name: Th2 cell
markers: IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13 (made by the cell)
No CXCR3 or CCR6 (human marker; tells it from Th1 and Th17 in blood)
summary: A helper T cell that organises defence against parasitic worms and other large parasites living outside cells, and that drives allergic inflammation. Steered by IL-4, it makes IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13. These call in eosinophils, make B cells switch to IgE, and trigger mucus and gut contractions that expel parasites.
functions: Develops in the lymph node from a naive CD4 T cell activated by a dendritic cell (in mice, a cDC2 subset) in the presence of IL-4, which switches on STAT6 and the transcription factor GATA3.
Debated: where the first IL-4 comes from. Basophils, other T cells and the developing Th2 cell itself have all been proposed, and the answer may depend on the type of response.

Makes IL-5, which recruits and activates eosinophils; IL-4 and IL-13, which with CD40L push B cells to switch to IgE antibody; and IL-13, which acts on epithelium and smooth muscle to cause mucus production and gut and airway contractions (the "weep and sweep" of worm expulsion).
Switches macrophages to an "alternative" state with IL-4 and IL-13 that helps repair tissue, wall off worms and limit damage. This is a repair programme, not a bacterial killing one.
Restrains competing helper cells: IL-4 steers naive CD4 T cells away from becoming Th1 cells (shown mainly in mouse experiments).
Drives allergy when its target is a harmless antigen such as pollen: IgE-armed mast cells and basophils, eosinophils and mucus then cause asthma or hay fever.
Debated: how much protection against worms depends on Th2 cells rather than on innate lymphoid cells, which make the same cytokines (IL-5, IL-13) earlier and without antigen recognition.
Debated: whether the help that makes B cells switch to IgE comes from Th2 cells or from IL-4-making Tfh cells inside follicles. The Tfh route has been shown in mice.
Leaves the lymph node, enters the blood and is drawn to tissues such as skin and lung by chemokines acting on CCR4.
abundance: A minority of memory CD4 T cells in the blood of healthy adults (CCR4-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative), higher in people with allergy or worm infection. Mouse strains differ: BALB/c mice favour Th2 responses, C57BL/6 mice favour Th1.
